Raigad Fort.history: Raigad Fort was the capital of the Maratha Empire under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in the 17th century. It is perched atop a 2700-foot hill in the Sahyadri range and is known for its strong fortifications, the grand Maha Darwaja gate, and the coronation throne of Shivaji Maharaj.

Rajgad Fort.history: Rajgad Fort served as the capital of the Maratha Empire for nearly 26 years before Raigad. Sitting atop a 4,600-foot hill, it is one of the largest hill forts in Maharashtra, famous for its three machis — Padmavati, Suvela, and Sanjeevani — and its massive fortification walls.

Pratapgad Fort.history: Pratapgad Fort is historically significant for the Battle of Pratapgad in 1659, where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj defeated Afzal Khan of the Adilshahi Sultanate. Located amidst dense forests near Mahabaleshwar, it has a two-level structure with the Bhavani Devi temple at its heart.

Ahmednagar Fort.history: Ahmednagar Fort is a large circular ground fort built in the 16th century by Hussain Nizam Shah I. It features twelve bastions and a surrounding moat. It later served as a prison during British rule, holding several Indian freedom fighters including Jawaharlal Nehru.

Lohagad Fort.history: Lohagad Fort is a hill fort famous for its distinctive Vinchukata — a narrow scorpion-tail shaped ridge path with four successive gates. It played an important role in the Maratha Empire as a treasury fort and is today a popular trekking destination near Pune.

Shivneri Fort.history: Shivneri Fort is the birthplace of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, born here in 1630. This triangular hill fort in Junnar has seven successive gates and strong defensive structures. It houses the Shivai Devi temple after which Shivaji was named.

Sindhudurg Fort.history: Sindhudurg Fort is a magnificent sea fort built by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1664–67 on a small island near Malvan. Constructed using coral stone and iron, it was built to establish Maratha naval supremacy. It uniquely houses handprints and footprints of Shivaji Maharaj.

Murud-Janjira Fort.history: Murud-Janjira Fort is a powerful island sea fort known for being unconquered despite attacks by the Marathas, Portuguese, and British. Built by the Siddi sultanate, it features 26 round bastions and rises directly from the Arabian Sea, accessible only by boat.

Vijaydurg Fort.history: Vijaydurg Fort is one of the oldest forts on the Konkan coast, situated where the Vaghotan river meets the Arabian Sea. Known as the Eastern Gibraltar of the Konkan, it has three concentric walls and served as the most important base for the Maratha navy.

Sinhagad Fort.history: Sinhagad Fort, formerly known as Kondana, is a historic hill fort near Pune famous for the Battle of Sinhagad in 1670, where Tanaji Malusare captured it for the Maratha Empire. Sitting atop the Bhuleswar range, it offers panoramic views of Khadakwasla lake and the Pune valley.

Daulatabad Fort.history: Daulatabad Fort, originally called Deogiri, is a 12th-century fort built on a perfectly conical rocky hill near Aurangabad. It is considered one of the most ingeniously designed forts in India, with a moat, a pitch-dark tunnel, and the iconic Chand Minar nearby. Muhammad bin Tughluq famously made it his capital in 1327.

Panhala Fort.history: Panhala Fort is one of the largest forts in the Deccan, situated near Kolhapur in the Sahyadri range. Built in the 12th century, it was an important stronghold of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj who spent a significant part of his life here. It is known for its Teen Darwaja, large granaries, and the famous escape of Shivaji to Vishalgad.
